title: Playing in white roadhouse bands before learning about color
summary: When shows got stranded he sat in with white roadhouse bands and says he did not learn about colored and white until 19 or 20.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: During those periods in different parts and places I've been and always running around, when the show gets stranded in what area - Chattanooga, Louisville, Paducah, or what area - they'd come over and ask me from those roadhouses, you come over and play in this band. I was integrating then. They knew me as Jo. I'd come in and play with these bands. I didn't know nothing about white and colored. I just thought it was music, just so nobody don't bother my drums, I knew where I'd stand. I didn't have to go and stay with Aunt Jane or Aunt Martha or whatever; I'd just stay in the place, you know. It didn't make much difference to me. And these guys were musicians.
I never knew about colored and white. I didn't know nothing about colored and white until I was 19 or 20.
